description: Edits a draft's recipients, subject, body or `send_at`. A future `send_at` schedules the draft to be sent then, and clearing it makes it a plain draft again. A draft that failed only because its agent was paused can be changed and scheduled again once the agent is resumed. Returns the draft.

bcc.description: Replaces the Bcc list, up to 50 addresses; `[]` empties it. Left out, it stays as it is.

body_html.description: Replaces the HTML body, up to 1,000,000 characters. Left out, it stays as it is.

body_text.description: Replaces the plain-text body, up to 1,000,000 characters. Left out, it stays as it is.

cc.description: Replaces the Cc list, up to 50 addresses; `[]` empties it. Left out, it stays as it is.

list_unsubscribe.description: Opt in to RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe: the message carries `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` headers, so the recipient's mail app shows an Unsubscribe button. One click suppresses the address for your whole workspace: every later send to it from any of your agents is refused with `recipient_suppressed` until you allowlist it (`POST /v1/suppression/allow`). Turn it on for newsletters, digests and other recurring mail. Leave it off (the default) for password resets, sign-in links, receipts and anything else the recipient must keep receiving. Needs exactly one `to` recipient and no `cc` or `bcc`.

send_at.description: A future time (ISO 8601, UTC, ending in `Z`) schedules the draft, and `null` unschedules it back to `draft`; left out, the schedule stays as it is. Setting a time needs the `send` scope, and a time not in the future is a 400.

subject.description: Replaces the subject, 1 to 998 characters. Left out, it stays as it is.

to.description: Replaces the recipients: one address, or a list of up to 50. Left out, they stay as they are.

name: mails_drafts_update
title: Update a draft
